audit.whatIsWrong: Three rows contradicted the packet chart and, worse, contradicted their own 'why' text: Level 1 read Aurora while whys[0] says her poke cannot out-trade your buckler; Level 3 read Poppy while whys[2] says it is 'genuinely even'; Level 6 read Aurora while whys[4] says you control every all-in.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Poppy/Skill/Skill/Poppy/Poppy/Poppy/Poppy and the mirror audit has already rebuilt Aurora's side to that same chart, so leaving ours as-is would put the two directions in direct conflict.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2 and 4 flipped in both layers as one group (Poppy, Skill, Poppy) with ratings moved to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns; the decisive spike was described only as 'level 6'.
audit.why: The real spike is a cooldown comparison: Steadfast Presence at 20s against Across the Veil at 22s means you get a window every rotation.
audit.corrected: 20s-vs-22s written into dosFull[0], report[5], whys[4], wants.you[1] and the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: Her escape was called 'her E blink' in eight places and her Q was repeatedly called a root. Across the Veil (W, 22s) is the leap that turns her invisible; The Weirding (E, 15s) is a blast that slows and hops her backward; Twofold Hex (Q, 9s) is a curse missile with a recast — there is no root anywhere in her kit.
audit.why: Riot's text is explicit on all three. Holding W for 'her E blink' means popping Steadfast Presence at the wrong ability entirely, and waiting to dodge a root that does not exist. Poppy's W does stop the W leap — that is the correct target, and stopping it grounds and slows her.
audit.corrected: Across the Veil named as the escape to stop, The Weirding as the slow-and-hop, and the phantom root removed in favour of the Twofold Hex recast.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing about Grievous Wounds, despite Spirit Abjuration healing her off every spell and attack.
audit.why: Riot's passive text: exorcised spirits follow her and heal her — that is the sustain that beats a Poppy grind trade.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal added to dontsFull[0] and report[5].

edits.before: Aurora's early game is poking with Q and respecting your E charge. At Level 1 you're both weak — just last-hit and don't eat free Q pokes by drifting into the minion line. Once you hit Level 2-3 with Q and E online your window opens: if she E-blinks aggressively or whiffs it, E her into the nearest wall for the stun and Q the max-HP chunk. Don't throw E on cooldown into open lane where she just blinks the carry distance clear — wait for her to commit her own dash first.
edits.after: Aurora's early game is Twofold Hex poke every 9s while respecting your E charge. At Level 1 you're both weak — last-hit and don't eat free curses by drifting into the minion line. Once Q and E are online your window opens: if she burns Across the Veil (W) aggressively, E her into the nearest wall for the stun and Q the max-HP chunk. Don't throw E on cooldown into open lane where she just leaps clear — make her commit the 22s W first.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 swing to you if you play the W bait right. Her only escape from your E charge is her E blink, so hold Steadfast Presence (W) — pop it as she blinks to ground the dash and stop her dead, then E her into the nearest wall for the stun. At 6 your R is a disengage/peel/displacement tool, not burst: use it to cancel her dive or hurl her off you if she lands a root, not as a kill button. Sidestep her Q-root setup from the brush and punish every blink she burns.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 swing to you if you play the W bait right. Her only escape from your E charge is Across the Veil (W) on 22s, and your Steadfast Presence is 20s — pop it as she leaps, which stops the dash and then grounds and slows her, and E her into the nearest wall. At 6 your R is peel and displacement, not burst: use it to cancel her dive or hurl her off you, not as a kill button. Sidestep the Twofold Hex recast and punish every leap she burns.

edits.before: You stay even-to-favored late because your kit is gold-independent: Q chunks her percent HP, W denies every blink and reposition, and an E-wall stun still yanks her out of position. She does get an AP item spike where her Q-root into E-W spirit combo can burst you if you facecheck it with no buckler shield up, so respect that one window. But she's a squishy skirmish-mage with no frontline — you out-sustain and out-disrupt her in any extended trade, and her root is the only tool that lets her kite you, so hold your W to ground the escape and never let her free-cast it.
edits.after: You stay even-to-favored late because your kit is gold-independent: Q chunks her percent HP, W stops every leap and reposition, and an E-wall stun still yanks her out of position. She does get an AP item spike where Twofold Hex into The Weirding can burst you if you facecheck it with no buckler shield up, so respect that window. But she's a squishy skirmish-mage with no frontline — and her spirits heal her, so anti-heal decides the grind. Hold W for Across the Veil and never let her free-cast the escape.

notes: The whole page was built on a phantom 'E blink' and a phantom Q root. Aurora's leap-and-invisibility escape is Across the Veil (W, 22s); The Weirding (E, 15s) slows and hops her backward; Twofold Hex (Q, 9s) curses and recasts, with no root in Riot's text. Following the mirror, I made no claim that Between Worlds cancels Keeper's Verdict — the hardCC flag on it is not supported by Riot's description. Three level-chart rows disagreed with their own why-text and with the packet chart; flipped as one group in both layers.
